cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest and a prophet, lives among the exiles by the River Kebar, and God has just told him to shut himself inside his house (Ezekiel 1:1-3; 2:5; 3:24). Now the Lord gives him a job, and friend, it starts with a brick. Not a scroll, not a trumpet, a BRICK.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to set a brick in front of him and draw on it the city of ___.

cards.text: City drawn, and now God tells Ezekiel to lay siege against it. Friend, I once laid siege to a stuck jar of sprinkles for a whole afternoon, and I LOST.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to build a ramp to the city on the brick and set up camps against it.

cards.text: Next, God tells Ezekiel to set up an iron plate as an iron wall between himself and the city, then turn his face toward it and besiege it.

cards.question: Ezekiel turns his face toward the city on the brick and besieges it. God says this will be what for the house of Israel?

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel to lie down on his LEFT side and bear the iniquity of the house of Israel, 390 days, one for each year of their iniquity. Friend, I can't stay on one side through a single snooze button.

cards.question: After those days, God tells Ezekiel to lie down again and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. Which way does he lie this time?

cards.text: God sets the count for this side at 40 days. Friend, that's finishing a double shift and hearing your boss say, “Great, now the other register.”

cards.question: Like his days for Israel, each of Ezekiel's 40 days for Judah stands for one year.

cards.text: God tells Ezekiel to keep his face turned toward the siege of Jerusalem, with his arm bared. Eyes locked on that brick, like me staring through the oven window at the last batch of the night.

cards.question: With his face toward the siege of Jerusalem and his arm bared, what is Ezekiel to do?

cards.text: Then God adds one more thing. He says, “Now behold, I will tie you up with ropes…”

cards.question: Before the days of his siege are finished, Ezekiel can roll over to his other side whenever he gets tired.

cards.text: Now God gives Ezekiel the menu for his 390 days on his side: wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt, all made into bread for himself.

cards.question: God gives Ezekiel six ingredients for his bread. How does He tell him to put them together?

cards.text: One container, one bread, and God has Ezekiel weigh out twenty shekels of it a day. Friend, I can't even weigh out chocolate chips without eating half of them off the scale.
His water gets measured too, a sixth of a hin, drunk at set times. Friend, a SIXTH of anything has never been a lot.

cards.question: Ezekiel may eat his weighed-out food whenever he gets hungry.

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel how to bake it. He's to eat it like a barley cake, baked over dried human excrement, in the sight of the people.

cards.question: Then the LORD says, “This is how the Israelites will eat their defiled bread…” Where will they eat it?

answers.text: In the nations He will banish them to
In the courts of His holy temple
In the wilderness of Mount Sinai

cards.text: Now Ezekiel speaks up: “Ah, Lord GOD,” he says. I bet his stomach just dropped to the floor.

cards.question: Ezekiel tells God he has never defiled himself.
After Ezekiel tells God he has never defiled himself, God replies. What does God change?

answers.text: What he bakes his bread over
How many days he lies down
Which grains go in his bread

cards.text: So it's cow dung instead of human excrement. Then God tells Ezekiel what's coming: “Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem.”

cards.question: God says that in Jerusalem, people will anxiously eat bread rationed by ___.

cards.text: In despair, they will drink water by measure too. So they will lack food and water, and friend, this is a heavy word.

cards.question: As they lack food and water, God says the people of Jerusalem will be appalled at the sight of one another wasting away in their ___.
